name: Pambia
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Only comparative Zande-group studies and wordlists (Tucker & Bryan, De Calonne-Beaufaict) in Glottolog; no phonology/grammar of Pambia found.

sources.citation: Grambank entry pamb1243 (coders Jakob Lesage, Janis Reimringer), sources: Santandrea 1965; Tucker & Bryan 1966; Tucker & Hackett 1959
sources.note: Confirms that the entire descriptive base for Pambia is these three works; Grambank codes no stress features.

sources.citation: Baxter, P. T. W. & Butt, Audrey. 1953. The Azande and related peoples of the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan and Belgian Congo (Ethnographic Survey of Africa, East Central Africa 9). London: IAI.
sources.note: APAMBIA entry: Sudan group west of Tembura; Congo group 'speaks Zande and retains little knowledge of its ancestral language'; Pambia and Abarambo languages 'almost identical... linked with Zande' (Giorgetti); footnote: 'Fr. Giorgetti has also unpublished MSS. on the languages of the Pambia-Barambo and Huma-Babuker.' Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: de Calonne-Beaufaict, Adolphe. 1921. Azande: introduction à une ethnographie générale des bassins de l'Ubangi-Uele et de l'Aruwimi. Bruxelles: Lamertin.
sources.note: Ethnography/history; Apambia named c. 28 times (e.g. p. 91: location on the Buere/Yubo, 'Le nom Apambia peut être traduit par: ceux de la chose de la pierre'); no linguistic description, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Tucker, A. N. & Bryan, M. A. 1966. Linguistic Analyses: The Non-Bantu Languages of North-Eastern Africa. London: OUP for IAI (Routledge Library Editions reprint 2017). Zande Group chapter, §2 'Tone and Stress'.

sources.harvard_location: WID Old Widener 2235.4.26; LIN GEN CoPh 36.88
sources.note: Contains the only located stress paragraph for the Zande group (Zande first-syllable stress; Barambu variants; 'stress never falls on prefixes') in the chapter where Pambia data are presented; the full page is needed to confirm whether Pambia is included or excepted and to get the page number.

sources.citation: Santandrea, Stefano. 1965. Languages of the Banda and Zande groups: A contribution to a comparative study. Napoli: Istituto Universitario Orientale. 254 pp.

sources.note: Glottolog's sole descriptive reference for [pmb]; comparative sketch with a Pambia-Barambu section and a tone discussion ('Tone plays an important role in all these languages'); needs reading for any stress remark.

sources.citation: Tucker, A. N. avec la collaboration de P. E. Hackett. 1959. Le groupe linguistique zande. Tervuren: Annales du Musée royal du Congo belge, Sciences de l'homme, Linguistique 22. 285 pp.

sources.note: Primary group description with grammatical notes on Pambia (abbrev. P.) and comparative vocabulary; index shows 'accent d'intensité' only for Zande pp. 48-49 and Barambu p. 179, so the Pambia notes must be read to confirm silence on stress and to see whether Pambia is folded into the Barambu statement.

sources.citation: Boyd, Raymond & Pasch, Helma. 1988. Le groupe zande. In Yves Moñino (ed.), Lexique comparatif des langues oubanguiennes, 59-64 + wordlists. Paris: Geuthner.

sources.note: Glottolog's subclassification reference for Pambia; comparative Ubangian lexicon with tone-marked Zande-group forms; may carry a short phonological note on Pambia (tone/stress) from Boyd's fieldwork.
